androidDownloadCheckpoint.scope: Sections 35 and 64: encrypted principal- and Session-bound disk checkpoints and explicit same-version continuation in Android core; application download adoption remains open
limitations: FileNativeDownloadStore leases one transfer exclusively and binds encrypted metadata to Host id, pinned fingerprint, device id, Session and requested path. Authenticated frames bind a random transfer id, sequence, offset and EOF. Callers must supply an authenticating cipher and explicit window/content limits; total content limits exclude encryption and framing overhead.

Synced encrypted frames precede atomic replacement of a synced encrypted checkpoint. Restore validates every committed frame, ignores uncommitted tail bytes, and preserves corrupt bytes. Explicit append truncates only the uncommitted tail. Complete copying decrypts one bounded frame at a time and requires consumer cleanup if copying fails after earlier output.

NativeDownloadController restores local state without network access. Explicit resume re-stats the descriptor and starts at the committed offset; changed path/version/size stops continuation. Preview and download share NativeResourceWire parsing for offsets, canonical base64, bounded progress and EOF. Close cancels and awaits request/disk work before releasing the lease.

interruptedTransfer.scope: Interrupted-transfer recovery matrix for complete-byte reads (specification section 35): when the Host advertises workspace-files.read-bytes.v1, Preview complete-byte loads run as fixed 1 MiB readBytes windows — bytes/transfer.ts provides the pure pieces (base64 window decoding, arrival-order assembly, a window constant at or below the Host default cap) and the face drives the loop under read generations, announcing each settled window through transferProgress. Open: same-candidate real-device verification and content-based MIME inference for unknown extensions
limitations: A resumed transfer continues from the first missing byte only while the tab lives; closing the tab drops the received prefix, and the recovery matrix is keyless-test proven, not yet real-device proven.

Manifest — one row per entry: stable bundle path plus the SHA-256 of its canonical key-sorted serialization. Checksum — one chained SHA-256 over the ordered manifest rows. Collector validation — recomputes every digest, refuses count mismatch, missing entries, tampering, unsorted manifests, and chain breaks. Input order never leaks (entries and manifest sort by path), so four platforms running the same candidate produce byte-identical bundles; determinism is pinned by a test. The wire types live on the ./types outlet with JsonValue content (typert refuses unconstrained unknown at the Remote boundary)

keyboardAvoidance.scope: Keyboard avoidance (spec section 8 second boundary): the AppFrame subscribes to window.visualViewport (resize and scroll) and, while the keyboard covers the viewport — scale 1 with the visible height under the window height — pins the frame element to the visible height, so the conversation bottom, including the composer, rides above the on-screen keyboard (iOS keyboard, Android IME, or a floating keyboard); when the keyboard closes, or under pinch zoom (which also shrinks the visual viewport but is zoom, not occlusion), the inline height clears and the stylesheet box returns. Runtime null/undefined visualViewport folds into one guard, so jsdom and older browsers mount untouched. Five jsdom cases hold the behavior through a stubbed visual viewport with live listeners: pinning while covered and following further resizes, clearing on keyboard close, ignoring pinch zoom until scale returns to 1, mounting without a visual viewport, and clearing the pinned height on unmount (packages/client/ui-layout). Section 8 traceability row refreshed honestly: rotation and foldable remain open
limitations: The pinning heuristic (scale 1 and visible height below the window height) distinguishes keyboards from pinch zoom, but a real-device pass over the iOS keyboard, Android IME, and a floating keyboard remains open — no physical device on this host.
